options.text: Write $5^{3} \times 5^{4} = 5^{7}$, adding the exponents because the bases are the same.
Write $5^{3} \times 7^{4} = 5^{7}$, adding the exponents even though the bases are not the same.
Choose $5^{7}$ only because $7$ is the largest single digit among $5$, $3$, and $4$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: For the same base, multiply powers by adding exponents: $5^{3}\times5^{4}=5^{7}$.

teacher.key_rationale: Same-base product adds exponents. Applying the rule when bases differ drops the same-base condition. Picking 7 from the printed digits captures a surface number.
